text: The bank has a board-approved cybersecurity strategy that includes ransomware preparedness.
Cybersecurity roles and responsibilities are assigned at senior-management level.
Cybersecurity risk is included in enterprise risk management.
The bank provides adequate budget and resources for ransomware preparedness.
Third-party and supply-chain cybersecurity risks are governed through policy.
The bank monitors relevant cybersecurity and privacy obligations.
Cybersecurity performance is reported to the board or executive committee.
The bank maintains an inventory of hardware, software, data and cloud assets.
Critical banking applications and sensitive information are identified and categorised.
Ransomware-focused risk and vulnerability assessments are performed regularly.
Dependencies on third-party vendors and service providers are mapped.
The bank considers cyber threats enabled by artificial intelligence.
The risk register includes ransomware scenarios.
Cybersecurity maturity is assessed against NIST CSF or a comparable framework.
Multi-factor authentication is enforced for privileged and remote access.
Patch management is implemented effectively.
Endpoint security or EDR is deployed across applicable endpoints.
Network segmentation is used to restrict ransomware spread.
Least-privilege access is implemented.
Cybersecurity awareness training is provided regularly.
Sensitive data is encrypted appropriately.
Backups are protected using offline, immutable or isolated controls.
Cybersecurity due diligence is performed on third-party vendors.
Email or web filtering is used to reduce ransomware delivery vectors.
Networks and endpoints are monitored continuously for anomalies.
A security operations capability or equivalent monitoring function exists.
Threat intelligence is used to identify ransomware campaigns.
Unauthorised data-exfiltration attempts can be detected.
Third-party access is monitored for suspicious activity.
Detections exist for ransomware indicators such as mass encryption or shadow-copy deletion.
Detection capabilities are assessed through controlled simulation exercises.
A documented ransomware incident-response plan exists.
Incident-response training or tabletop exercises are conducted.
Cybersecurity incident communication and escalation procedures are defined.
Affected systems can be isolated rapidly during an incident.
Forensic and legal support arrangements are defined.
The bank can coordinate with regulators, law enforcement and affected third parties.
Crisis-communication procedures address customers and media.
A formally approved ransom-payment policy exists.
Backup recovery processes are practised for critical systems.
Banking operations can be restored within approved recovery-time objectives.
Post-incident reviews produce control improvements.
Alternative locations or cloud recovery arrangements exist.
Recovery strategies are improved using lessons learned.
Ransomware recovery tests are conducted at planned intervals.
Recovery activities are coordinated with relevant third parties.
The bank assesses risks from AI-powered phishing or social engineering.
Automation supports detection of ransomware or phishing where appropriate.
Security training addresses AI-enabled attacks.
The bank monitors AI-enabled vulnerability discovery and exploitation trends.
